Jeep Announces Everything That's New For the 2027 Gladiator: New Base Model, Fresh Features and More
8 photos
Photo: Jeep
Stellantis is making sure that Jeep gets the spotlight this fall season and has implemented a 'what's new' style series for its 2027MY upgrades and updates. We’ve already seen the novelties for the Wrangler and Cherokee, and now it’s Gladiator’s turn.
In fact, Jeep has raised the bar for the mid-size premium adventure pickup truck a little further than before – they also announced the “most requested upgrade” now arrives straight from the factory for the first time: the 2027 Tire Launch Edition features 35-inch all-terrain tires from the factory on Willys, Rubicon, and Rubicon X models.
Additionally, there’s a brand-new entry-level Sport S model starting from an MSRP of $43,895 (sans the $1,995 destination), which makes the Gladiator more expensive than last year after the deletion of the Sport version. Now there are only eight models to configure instead of 12, by the way, and the Sport S has gone up in price by $880 compared to the 2026 model year.
At least now the 2027 Jeep Gladiator Sport S comes with a standard seven-inch TFT color instrument cluster, passive entry, all-terrain tires, and 17-inch machined aluminum wheels. The Sahara, which is now $48,400 instead of $48,115, comes standard with a vented power dome hood and side steps, and there’s also an optional premium wheel package which adds machined 20-inch wheels with all-terrain tires, heavy-duty Dana 44 axles, and a Trac-Lok limited-slip rear differential.
Moving on, the Rubicon and Mojave models are now $55,700 and $56,200, respectively, instead of $53,215 both, and have standard body-color fender flares, heated front seats, heated steering wheel, as well as embedded navigation. Further up the scale, the Rubicon X and Mojave X packages ($64,180 and $63,295, respectively, instead of $61,210 both) now add the standard cargo management group. It consists of a 115V bed power outlet, roll-up tonneau cover, lockable and removable rear under-seat storage bin, and bed-mounted Trail Rail System.
Now, a standard black hardtop comes on the Willys and Rubicon, while Mojave has a body-color hardtop; the Gladiator Altitude, based on the Sport S, comes with black 20-inch wheels with all-terrain tires, wide-track Dana 44 heavy-duty axles, Trac-Lok limited-slip rear differential, dark accents, and an optional performance hood. Meanwhile, the Sahara gets the High Altitude back with machined 20-inch wheels with all-terrain tires, body-color bumpers, mirrors, door and tailgate handles, Nappa leather seats, as well as wide-track Dana 44 heavy-duty axles, a Trac-Lok limited-slip rear differential, and an available performance hood. It comes in Black, Bright White, and Sting-Gray only.
Also, the Jeep Performance Parts (JPP) Mojave, based on the Desert Rated Gladiator Mojave, comes with a flurry of Mopar accessories, including a triple-hoop grille guard, hood graphics, black grille, multi-accessory rail, cold-air intake, all-weather floor mats, an 83-piece tool kit, and Camel Katzkin leather seats featuring Terracotta stitching and embroidery. All versions are powered by the well known 3.6-liter V6 engine, packing 285 hp and 260 lb.-ft. of torque, fitted only with the eight-speed automatic transmission.

source_document.body:
Britain will not join the Canada-led Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, in a setback to efforts to create the world’s first global defense bank, according to a person familiar with the matter.
The two countries instead said on Sunday that they would develop a framework for cooperation between their respective defense-funding initiatives, establishing two distinct but complementary institutions to support each other on investment opportunities and strategic challenges.
“We have been working closely to consider how the Multilateral Defence Mechanism (MDM) and Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB) can best advance our shared objectives,” the statement said.
The two governments were unable to agree on key issues including the location of the headquarters of a joint institution, the level of joint procurement, lending to members, and the rules around new members, a second person said.
The MDM will focus on accelerating defense investment, joint procurement through financing, and bringing together demand across NATO allies to reduce procurement costs, while the DSRB will complement it by supporting investment in defense industries and supply chains, focusing more on single sovereign lending, the person added.
The DSRB, which will be based in Canada, has faced challenges securing support from larger European nations. Reuters was first to report in September last year that Britain had declined to join the project.
There were hopes Britain would reconsider its position under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his team. Germany had previously declined to join. A spokesperson for the German finance ministry said Germany was an observer in the negotiations on DSRB’s charter and is reviewing open questions.
Britain and Canada said the MDM and DSRB will be designed to work in close partnership, so they can support each other on emerging industrial priorities, investment opportunities and strategic financing challenges.
The DSRB has been aiming to raise around €100 billion ($112 billion) and use the money to lend at low cost to governments and contractors for defense projects. It will also offer guarantees for lenders financing smaller firms seen as riskier borrowers.
So far Albania, Belgium, Greece, Latvia, Luxembourg, Romania, Turkey and Ukraine have pledged their support, along with Canada.
Canadian Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said the group would meet in Luxembourg on Nov. 30 to sign articles of agreement establishing the bank.
“Membership (is) open to other allies and close partners who share the Bank’s objective,” he said in a statement.
Reuters previously reported that potential members had not joined because of concerns including whether the DSRB can offer cheaper financing than highly rated national governments as well as the amount of capital countries would need to commit, the bank’s governance, and overlaps with existing initiatives.
Britain’s Defence Secretary Wes Streeting had recently described the DSRB as a “really interesting and innovative mechanism” and said that he did not see the proposed defense bank and MDM as being in competition.
Britain previously declined to join, citing concerns over value for money. Reuters previously reported that Burnham discussed the DSRB alongside the MDM initiative with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in July and with Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden during an August visit to Kyiv.

No New Widowmaker From Porsche? No Problem With SSR Performance’s Project Leo!
13 photos
Photo: Baldauf
As you likely know, there hasn’t been a 911 GT2 RS in Porsche’s lineup ever since the 991.2, aka the previous generation that was retired back in late 2019. And that’s despite the constant rumors that this model will eventually be back with an even more impressive bang in the company’s portfolio.
However, the tuning world is so advanced today that it can easily step in and fill certain voids. You know, like the lack of a modern-day Porsche 911 GT2 RS. And this is where SSR Performance comes in. The German tuner, which also has some very important motorsport ties, is currently preparing a monstrous project that is a 911 but isn’t one at the same time. And this makes us wonder whether there is indeed room in today’s automotive game for something like this.
But all in due course, as first, we have to put the spotlight on the vehicle itself. It is called the Project Leo, and our spy photographers report that it is based on the latest Porsche 911 GT3 RS . You know, as in the 992.2. And guess what? It indeed appears to build on this model, as some of the aero is definitely there, though it has been significantly altered to the point where this thing looks like a track monster.
The changes are obvious, as there is a new bumper at the front, complete with an adjustable apron, and the front hood appears to have been tweaked. We can also see some flaps on the sides of the front bumper, as well as new trim for the air intakes behind the doors. More updates are visible at the rear, where the bumper is under wraps, and we can clearly see that it is entirely new, and likely a lot more aerodynamic than the OEM element.
Photo: Baldauf The diffuser may look like a mess, more or less, but this part is likely not finished. Or at least the tailpipes aren’t, and we can see four of them, two on each side of the rear license plate holder. It looks like a new aero brake is also on deck, and from what we can tell, that massive wing that sits on the rear deck has also been modified. The wheels are part of the novelties, and so is the trim on the rear three-quarter windows, among other things.
Mind you, the aero bits and pieces would be nothing without a power boost, and rumor has it that the SSR Performance’s Project Leo might also have more oomph compared to the standard Porsche 911 GT3 RS . The latter has 518 hp (525 ps/386 kW) and 343 lb-ft (465 Nm) of torque from its naturally aspirated 4.0-liter flat-six engine, taking 3.2 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph), and 10.6 seconds to reach 124 mph (200 kph) from a standstill.
It will do 50-75 mph (80-120 kph) in just 1.8 seconds, and if you keep the right pedal pinned to the floor, then the odometer will eventually read 184 mph (296 kph). The Project Leo should be even more extreme than the regular Porsche 911 GT3 RS, as word on the street is that SSR Performance has strapped two turbochargers to the flat-six motor mentioned above. Naturally, we have to learn how much the tuned mill develops, and how fast the car is, yet these aspects will be revealed in due course, likely during the grand unveiling.
Photo: Baldauf SSR Performance’s Project Leo won’t be fast for nothing, because it looks like the company may want to set a new lap record on the Nurburgring Nordschleife. As you likely remember, Manthey’s 911 GT2 did 6:43.300 some five years ago. However, that model is not exactly a direct rival to this modded 911 GT3 RS, because that would be the mighty Mercedes-AMG One, which completed the course in 6:29.090 a couple of years ago.
As a result, SSR Performance needs to beat the German hypercar’s time if it wants to become the new King of the ‘Ring, and we reckon it might be able to do that. After all, we are looking at a very crazy Porsche 911 GT3 RS , presumably with twin turbocharging, as well as more advanced aerodynamics, and, between us, we cannot wait to see whether the company manages to do that.
Details surrounding the official unveiling date are also unknown at this point, though if we were to bet, we’d probably say that the Project Leo from SSR Performance could officially come out of hiding either before the end of the year or in the first half of 2027. And when it does, chances are it will have already lapped the Nurburgring Nordschleife, fighting the clock in order to become the fastest of the fastest.
But is there really room on the market today for a crazy Porsche 911 that’s not exactly a 911 ? Drop your comments below in the dedicated section and tell us all about it.

All-New 2027 Grand Design Solitude 394RO Is a Fifth-Wheel RV That Does Everything Differently
19 photos
Photo: The RV Hunter
You know how some people say some things are " to die for " and you tend to roll your eyes at how dramatic they are? Well, the 2027 Solitude 394RO, a brand-new floorplan from Grand Design RV (GDRV), could be one of those things: a fifth-wheel RV that tackles extended RV-ing with a fresh approach in almost every aspect that matters.
GDRV has been in the business of luxury for long enough to know what works and what doesn't, and the reason they've been in the business this long is their willingness to change to grow. The 2027 model year for the Solitude series of luxury fifth wheels means not just a complete redesign, from top to bottom, but the addition of brand-new floorplans.
This is where the Solitude 394RO comes in, a floorplan so new it's not even featured yet on the manufacturer's website. But GDRV has been showing it off to select media and dealers, which means that we, too, can have a proper look at it even before all the numbers are official.
One such look comes via the extended video tour available at the bottom of the page, courtesy of The RV Hunter . Shot this month at a trade event, it highlights a luxury fifth wheel RV that does everything differently, from construction to finishes and the kind of amenities available.
Photo: The RV Hunter That's no exaggeration, either. Designed for extended, year-round living, the Solitude 394RO packs every feature you might need or even imagine you might need onboard, inside a package that's beautifully luxurious, high-quality, and residential-like.
You have sleeping for as many as six people with this floorplan , but also two kitchens, a full bathroom with a soaking tub, a beautifully appointed kitchen, a main bedroom with storage galore, and a dedicated office. You also have a side patio with that second kitchen, excellent HVAC, and the kind of construction that GDRV likes to pride themselves in being the only one to offer it.
That starts with the Lippert Omega FifthWheel frame, which comes with a five-year extended warranty, and continues with a reinforced structure, a marine-grade fiberglass body injected for color, and the TekModo Worry-Free Composite Roof System with zero seams. They use the same kind of roofing for the four slide-outs, which also come with laminated sidewalls.
Photo: The RV Hunter The Solitude 394RO features large frameless tinted windows, dual entries if you count the sliding glass door to the patio, and a redesigned front cap. It rides on a tandem axle with H-rated tires with TMPS, MORryde independent suspension, and disc brakes.
Coming in at a total length of 42 feet 10 inches (13 meters), this fifth wheeler sits on a widebody 101-inch (256-cm) chassis, which explains the residential feel of space inside. The layout is partly inspired by the successful Solitude 414LJM but adapted to the needs of those RV-ers who might want to mix business with pleasure and get some work done on the road.
That's where the "RO" (rear office) comes in. It's the highlight of the floorplan, specced with a motorized sit-stand oversize desk facing the huge rear window, but it can easily double as a guest bedroom or a mancave of sorts, whether that be a games' room or an extra lounge.
Photo: The RV Hunter It also features a nice pull-out sofa, dedicated storage , a full-body mirror, and a large-screen TV with more hidden storage behind it. As far as home offices go, this is far better than anything you'll find in other manufacturers.
The rest of the layout maintains a typical fifth wheel design, which means that the main entrance gives into the kitchen and dining space, while the main bedroom is on the upper deck. GDRV uses that front cap to build a very useful walk-in wardrobe at the front, complete with a separate closet for a washer and dryer.
Where the layout might be typical for a fifth wheel, the design is anything but. GDRV uses residential furniture and cabinetry, full-size appliances, and a fresh take on almost every feature to create a space that's truly unmatched.
Photo: The RV Hunter The kitchen features a peninsula that slides and extends at camp, complete with an oversize sink, a pantry, and a built-in slide-out cutting board. A double-door XL fridge with water filtration and ice making capabilities is included, while the separate cooking block comes with a GE convection microwave airfryer, a four-burner gas cooktop, and a large oven.
The fact that you have everything from all the prep space you'd need, lots of storage, and even dedicated drawers for items like paper towels and recycling trash cans tells you that this RV is made for extended living.
The dinette is on the campsite side – a cozy nook for meals and games, complete with a floating table, a pair of chairs, and a more comfortable bench seating.
Photo: The RV Hunter From the kitchen, you transition into the spacious living room , specced with a sectional sofa with integrated ottomans and reclining theater seats, all of which can be used to form a giant bed. A large-screen TV sits on a contrasting panel wall, above an electric fireplace.
The patio is a drop-down one, and it comes standard with a power awning and an integrated kitchen, specced with another large-screen TV, a stainless-steel sink, all-aluminum cabinetry, and a small drinks fridge. The TV is a rather too close to the sink for comfort, but if you plan to use the latter only occasionally, it shouldn't be an issue.
The bathroom is on the upper deck, in front of the bedroom. It's a decent-sized one, perhaps to compensate for the fact that there's only one onboard for six people, with a nice tub with fiberglass surround, a skylight, and a shower curtain. Solid surface counters, another stainless steel sink, a porcelain toilet, and plenty of storage options are also standard .
Photo: The RV Hunter The bedroom puts a king bed in the slide-out and a dresser with another fireplace and another smart TV on a televator across from it. GDRV builds in storage under the bed, in the form of drawers and oversize large trays that you can pull out and load with boxes or shoes.
Standard features include 660W of solar on the roof for extended autonomy, a four-season package, three 18,000-BTU Furrion Chill Cube ACs with heat pumps, a furnace, two fireplaces, a Fogatti on-demand water heater, hydraulic auto-leveling, an upgraded MORryde pinbox, three power awnings with LED lights, and two large storage compartments.
One of these is a pass-through basement made possible with the drop-down frame, while the other is the rear compartment built under the office space and equipped with a MORryde storage tray and extra access points.
Photo: The RV Hunter Numbers made public so far include the size of the holding tanks (83 gallons/314 liters for fresh, 159 gallons/602 liters for gray, and 53 gallons/200 liters for black) and the gross weight (23,500 lbs/10,569 kg). Everything else is still TBD (to be determined), including pricing .
As a reference only, a Solitude has a starting MSRP of $158,788, so yes, you're looking at a truly premium product .
Via // The RV Hunter

VW’s Tiguan R Spied, It’s a High-Riding Golf R
12 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | CarSpyMedia
As the third generation Tiguan turns two, Volkswagen is preparing its most exciting version, the one that adds the R suffix.
Spied on a few occasions earlier this year, the model will sit at the very top of the family, and as you likely know, it will be a forbidden fruit in North America. Why is that, you ask? Well, because the Tiguan that Volkswagen sells over here is nothing more than Europe’s rebadged Tayron. In theory, the company could come up with a similar product for the New World. After all, the two share the same underpinnings, namely the VW Group’s MQB Evo platform. In practice, however, there will be no Tayron R.
Our latest encounter with the Volkswagen Tiguan R came via CarSpyMedia on YouTube, and shows a couple of prototypes of the sporty crossover attacking the Nurburgring and driving on the roads right next to the famous German racetrack. The differences between the top-of-the-line flavor of the series and the regular ones are quite subtle, at first glance, anyway, because if you compare them, then you will quickly see that the Tiguan R looks a lot more aggressive than its lesser siblings.
For instance, there is an entirely new bumper at the front, with redesigned air intakes, a different pattern for the lower grille, and much chunkier integrated diffuser. The upper grille should also be different, albeit not by much, and the headlights and the thin light strip linking them together will likely carry over with no changes. The same goes for the corporate logo that interrupts the lights strip right in the middle, as well as the hood, and the front fenders.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | CarSpyMedia From what we can tell, the side skirts of the Volkswagen Tiguan R have been tweaked, and they are now finished in the same color as the rest of the body. However, the black plastic trim on the wheel arches is still there. The side mirrors, doors, windows, and roof rails are also the same, to no one’s surprise. Out back, the model retains the same taillights, tailgate, and even the Tiguan emblem below the license plate holder, and even the roof spoiler appears to be the same.
However, the biggest changes lie further down, as the model features quad exhaust tips, and they are apparently part of the Akrapovic exhaust system. The wheels will also be on the special side of things, and the model sits a bit closer to the ground due to the new chassis setup. This will allow it to corner a bit faster than the regular third-gen VW Tiguan models, and will also make the ride a bit jigglier. Look for uprated brakes too, which will keep the extra oomph in check.
You do know what will power the Volkswagen Tiguan R , don’t you? That’s right, the same engine as the Golf R. The all-wheel drive compact hot hatch features a 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine, which is officially rated at 328 horsepower (333 ps/245 kW) and 295 pound-feet (400 Nm) of torque.
The lump is paired with a 7-speed DSG automatic transmission and R-Performance 4Motion all-wheel drive with torque vectoring, taking roughly four seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph), and maxing out at up to 168 mph (270 kph) with the optional Performance Pack. The top speed is electronically limited to 155 mph (250 kph) as standard. Due to the extra weight, the Tiguan R should be a bit slower, assuming that it retains the same output and thrust as its hot hatch sibling.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | CarSpyMedia Look for some changes on the inside, too, where the Volkswagen Tiguan R is expected to get a pair of bucket seats for the driver and front passenger, as well as a new steering wheel, and a different gear selector. The upholstery and trim should also be on the more special side of things, thus further helping this model stand out from its lesser siblings.
As we already told you, the Tiguan that Volkswagen sells in the United States of America is related to the Tayron marketed in Europe, so we are looking at two different products that wear the same name. This means that Europe’s Tiguan R won’t cross the Atlantic Ocean, and it is highly unlikely that the Tayron would also get the R treatment, so there will be no sporty version of the Tiguan destined for the New World.
We have yet to learn when Volkswagen intends to officially pull the wraps off the new Tiguan R, but word on the street is that the presentation could be right around the corner, and some outlets believe that it might take place sometime this fall. If that’s the case, then the first units of the sporty crossover could end up at dealers overseas either before the end of the year or in early 2027.
Would you have wanted something like this on our shores?

Fourth-Gen Peugeot 308 Gets Radical Virtual Fastback Makeover Inspired by Paris Motor Show Concepts
9 photos
Photo: avarvarii / Instagram
Stellantis wanted to show that it cares about classic automotive shows, and since the 2026 Mondial de l’Auto is considered as one of its home turf events, it arrived in full force with over 60 new vehicles and no less than nine concepts among them.
They even organized a ‘The Night Before’ event, just like during the good old days before Covid, where they presented six of the prototypes ahead of the official reveal in front of the general audience. Most of the important brands got their five minutes of fame in front of the 2026 Paris Motor Show spotlights at the Paris Expo Porte de Versailles venue, and of course the French brand Peugeot was a chief among them.
More precisely, the near-premium French marque showcased two concepts, the RCZ Vision and the E-T16 , with the first one bringing back the RCZ double-bubble-roofed coupe for a new stint and the other paying homage to the Peugeot 205 T16 in a retro-futuristic hot hatch manner with ludicrous EV power. Both of them are brand manifestos, revealing the new design direction the French brand is about to take.
Sure, they might also become real, reviving the RCZ and paving the way for an EV to rival the bonkers Renault 5 Turbo 3E hot hatchback. But it’s more likely that most of their styling elements will trickle down to regular models – including the upcoming fourth generation of the Peugeot 308 compact car, at least according to the rumor mill.
More precisely, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI has worked for the rumor mill to uncover the new generation’s digital secrets in their latest unofficial, hypothetical design project. Andrei Avarvarii, the virtual artist behind Avarvarii Automotive Artworks (also known as ' avarvarii ' on social media), has taken a thorough, in-depth CGI look at Peugeot's upcoming plans for the good folks over at Auto Express and came up with this virtual proposition.
Because we have already seen that some of the latest Peugeot models like the 408 or even the latest 3008 have slightly wackier designs than usual, “these illustrations envision a bold new direction for the next-generation Peugeot 308.” According to the author and the publication, “rather than retaining its traditional two-box hatchback proportions, the design transitions into a sleek, aerodynamic fastback.”
Inspiration comes from the Peugeot Inception and the two Paris Motor Show concepts, but also from the larger 408, so “the front fascia features a sharp, angular profile, a seamless body-colored grille, and a razor-thin evolution of the brand's signature three-claw LED lighting.” Sculpted geometric elements adorn the sides, along with aero-optimized wheels and a raked roofline, while the back has a “muscular, high-set tail.”
The new triple-layer full-width LED taillights are also present, in an interpretation set between the serious E-T16 and the exotic RCZ Vision concept. As for powertrains, the news outlet muses that the new STLA One platform will make it EV -first but also capable of gasoline and hybrid setups if needed. The new model will probably feature the new cockpit architecture inside as well as the pioneering ‘cell-to-body’ setup where the battery is part of the floor structure like in BYD or Tesla models, among others. This 23FT Low-Profile Motorhome Has the Largest Bathroom and Garage of Its Class
27 photos
Photo: Pilote
It's the little things that make a difference, as the saying goes. In the case of this compact low-profile motorhome, this is more than a marketing phrase being thrown around to attract attention, but the ethos on which it's built.
This is the Pilote P690D motorhome from French specialist Pilote , now at its 2027 model year. Introduced for 2020, this is just one of the many floorplans available in the Pacific range that gives the "P" in the official moniker, but also the smallest entry available in the Evidence specification.
Pilote offers two configurations for the Pacific motorhomes: the basic Expression spec and the all-include Evidence. Obviously, not all floorplans can be ordered as an Evidence, which allows the P690D to stand out as the most compact yet still fully functional entry of the four available for 2027.
Technicalities aside, what the casual observer might take away from this motorhome is the fact that, despite its relative compact dimensions, it's able to offer the biggest bathroom and the biggest garage of its class. It also offers a nice galley kitchen, ready for decent meals on vacation, a gorgeous and very spacious lounge, and sleeping for four – all of whom will have belted seats for safe and legal transport.
Photo: Pilote The way Pilote is able to deliver all these is by erasing the fixed bed. So, yes, this motorhome is ideal only for those who don't feel like having a fixed bed is a deal-breaker. You still get a comfortable double bed and even a second convertible one underneath, but they both come into sight only when you need them, at night, leaving the floorspace open for living and entertaining during the day.
The P690D Evidence is based on the 140-hp Fiat Ducato chassis with automatic transmission and is designed as an "all-inclusive" package, so you get items you'd have to upgrade for (an awning, alloy wheels, backup camera) as standard.
The RV comes in at 7.02 meters (23 feet) in length and 2.3 meters (7.5 feet) in width, being rated for a maximum permissible weight of 3,500 kg (7,716 lbs), of which 360 kg (793 lbs) will be solely payload. That means you can operate it on a standard B Category driving license , while making the most out of all the available storage space.
Photo: Pilote That's what actually new for 2027, as Pilote points out. The redesigned interior allows for more volume inside without sacrificing any of the creature comforts fans of this particular floorplan have come to love. In fact, everything about the P690D feels new, from the upholstery to the redesigned kitchen and the redesigned wardrobe at the rear.
Indeed, this is a rare example of a European compact motorhome with an integrated wardrobe – and we're not talking just a cramped closet you can hang two shirts in.
At the back, on top of the spacious and height-adjusting garage, Pilote adds a full wardrobe with a stack of shelves on one side and generous hanging space on the other. You also get drawers below and, farther down, a direct pass-through connection to the garage.
Photo: Pilote The best part is that you get all these with minimal compromise in terms of the size or functionality of the bathroom. This is a full-width room with a cassette toilet on the campside and a small vanity with sink and integrated storage, and a nice shower cubicle across the way. With this disposition, you still get ample free floorspace to use as a dressing room, while you rummage through the wardrobe in search of the perfect 'fit.
The middle section of the RV is the kitchen, divided into two blocks, as is standard in this class in the EU: the main cooking block and the fridge and storage across the way. While compact and under-specced by U.S. standards, this galley still stands out for how elegant and nice it is.
Standard features include a separate sink, a two-burner cooktop with a glass cover, black backsplash to match the black hardware, an accent wall with storage hooks, underbody accent lights, and plenty of storage options. This is a small space to cook elaborate meals in, but it's spacious enough to let you move freely without bumping into stuff or, even worse, knocking over pots and pans.
Photo: Pilote The lounge is another highlight of this floorplan, made more striking with the new upholstery and lighter cabientry. Pilote says you can comfortably sit six people around the two-leaf solid table, but you could probably squeeze in as many as eight, thanks to the cushy, oversize benches in a face-to-face arrangement.
At night, this dinette can convert into a double bed, but you have to keep in mind that the main double bed will drop down over it. A family of four not adverse to the idea of sleeping in bunkbeds would find this arrangement ideal, especially when considering what's gained through it – the garage space and the large bathroom with wordrobe.
Speaking of the garage, it now comes with a 1.75-meter (5.7-foot) high access hatch, adjustable height on either end so you can store taller items, separate open cubbies, tie-downs, an outdoor shower, and a light. It is, in short, ideal for those who travel with gear of all kinds or simply heavy packers.
Photo: Pilote The 2027 Pilote P690D Evidence carries 130 liters (34 gallons) of freshwater and 95 liters (25 gallons) of gray, as well as 90 liters (23.7 gallons) of fuel. Imagined as an "all-inclusive" package, it still allows for some customization in terms of interior colors and textures, and prices start at €78,900 ($88,000 at the current exchange rate) for the 2027 model year.

2026 SEMA Show: Mitsubishi Returns to Las Vegas With the Fresh 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition
14 photos
Photo: Mitsubishi
Mitsubishi Motors North America, Inc. ( MMNA ) revealed in advance of the 2026 edition of the SEMA Show (November 3-6) its return to Las Vegas, Nevada, for the first time since 2012 – they’re coming to celebrate the release of the all-new 2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition.
The Japanese automaker’s US subsidiary is a pale shadow of a shadow of its former self: earlier this month they reported a total of just 18,543 deliveries for the third quarter of 2026, and since then the only novelty has been the reveal of the pricing details for the Nissan Leaf-based 2027 Mitsubishi Eclipse Sportback, which starts at an MSRP of almost $38k, which is much higher than its corporate sibling.
Anyway, now Mitsubishi wants to steal the spotlight of the 2026 SEMA Show in advance, announcing the world debut of the 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition, a rugged, off-road-focused model designed to compete with the likes of the 2026 Toyota RAV4 Woodland and Subaru Forester Wilderness or Honda CR-V TrailSport and Ford Bronco Sport Badlands, among others.
It will mark the return of Mitsubishi to the SEMA Show as it will be the brand's first appearance at the premier automotive aftermarket event since 2012. The Mitsubishi Motors exhibit will be located at Booth 52249 in West Hall, and the headline will be the all-new 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition, dubbed as “the most capable and adventure-focused Outlander ever offered in North America.”
Mitsubishi aims to “expand its presence among adventure-minded customers and automotive enthusiasts” as part of the new Momentum 2030 business plan. Based on the strategy, six vehicles will be showcased at the event, from the factory-built adventure model to extreme customization concept builds “inspired by the brand's off-road heritage.”
After the recent global debut of the reborn Pajero, Mitsubishi aims to bring a new level of “ruggedness and confidence to North America's best-selling Mitsubishi nameplate” with the 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition. It will spearhead new off-road-capable vehicles, complete with “off-road-focused bodywork, all-terrain tires, revised approach and departure angles, and a new Rock drive mode to create the most capable Outlander ever offered.”
More precisely, the new Rock mode has upgraded brake control to rein in wheel-slip and help secure traction. It’s faster than in other modes of the S-AWC all-wheel drive system, and the driver also gets a new screen setting in the digital instrument cluster to showcase front-wheel steering angle, individual wheel-slip, and traction-control intervention. The Multi-View Camera System can stay on at up to 18.6 mph or 30 kph, and when the Rock Mode is selected, Hill Descent Control is automatically activated as well – adjustable “for the speed at which it holds the vehicle.”
The Outlander Diamond Trail Edition also gets a matte black grille, black Dynamic Shield trim, black finish headlights, and redesigned front and rear bumpers to improve the approach and departure angles from 18.3 to 20.5 degrees and from 22.2 to 23.1 degrees. There are also new over-fenders, unique 18-inch black alloy wheels, dedicated Nexen Roadian ATX all-terrain tires, as well as raised roof rails.
Inside, the Diamond Trail Edition gets a unique water-repelling dark grey material with khaki stitching, plus textured matte black, dark chrome and dark satin trim elements. The new Diamond Trail Edition logo – “intended to be representative of skilled athletes on a downhill course, and playing on the motif of the brand's Three Diamonds” - is applied to the seat backs, floor mats, and the door trim. Also, the Outlander Diamond Trail Edition comes with an all-new color: Trail Green Metallic.

Meet the First-Ever BMW X5 M Electric!
16 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
It’s been a few months since BMW pulled the wraps off the all-new fifth-generation X5 . The G65, or the G78 as you likely know the LWB (long wheelbase) model if you live in China, debuted back in June, 2026, and two months later, it hit the assembly line at the Spartanburg factory in South Carolina, USA, and at Dadong in the People’s Republic.
It’s not only the regular ICE model that debuted back then, but also the first fully electric X5. It is called the BMW iX5, to no one’s surprise, and unlike its internal combustion-powered sibling, it misses out on the air intakes between the license plate and kidney grille. During the grand unveiling, the company estimated an EPA range of 435 miles (700 km) with the 144 kWh battery pack fully charged.
BMW’s iX5 is officially coming to our market in 2027, the brand’s website reveals, and it packs quite a punch in the 60 AWD configuration. This model has a pair of electric motors that churn out a total of 570 horsepower (578 ps/425 kW) and 593 pound-feet (804 Nm) of torque. The BMW iX5 60 AWD takes only 4.4 seconds from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph). That’s 0.7 seconds slower than the old X5 M, which has 617 hp (625 ps/460 kW) and 553 lb-ft (750 Nm) of torque to play with from its twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8 engine.
As you likely know by now, an entirely new BMW X5 M, based on the G65 generation, is in the making as we speak. Word on the street is that it might pack the same powertrain as the latest M5, namely a plug-in hybrid 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8, which churns out a maximum of 717 hp (727 ps/535 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque in the business super sedan and wagon. The former takes 3.4 seconds from 0 to 62 mph (0-100 kph), and the latter does it in 3.5 seconds.
Photo: SH Proshots Due to the extra weight, because the future BMW X5 M will be heavier, not to mention more spacious, this model is expected to be a bit slower than the latest M5. You know, just like the current M5 is slower than its predecessor. And it will probably not be able to match the straight-line performance of the old X5 M.
And if the ICE BMW X5 M is not exactly to your liking, then you should know that the company is also preparing a battery-electric alternative to this model. The zero-emission X5 M has been caught testing on a few occasions, and it is now back under the limelight, courtesy of our man with the cam, who recently sent the images shared above in the gallery to our inboxes.
Word on the street is that the BMW X5 M Electric , or the iX5 M, whatever it will be named, might have in the region of 800 to 900 brake horsepower to play with. This equals 811-912 metric horsepower, and 596-671 kilowatts. Keep in mind that these numbers are not official, as nobody who is not directly involved in its development knows anything about the powertrain for now.
Photo: SH Proshots As far as the visual differences go, the scooped prototype featured an entirely new bumper with redesigned air intakes. The styling is visible even from beneath the trippy vinyl stickers. The grille appears to be new as well, and chances are that the headlights might feature fresh graphics. The wheel arches do not seem to be on the fat side of things, and from what we can tell, the side skirts do not look different either.
The same goes for the door mirrors, too, though you may want to keep in mind the fact that this is a tester, and these things could change once the model hits the assembly line. The rear bumper is also new, and you should ignore the reflectors, which are provisional. The wheels are also exclusive to the BMW X5 M Electric (or iX5 M), and they should hide an uprated braking system behind them. The chassis setup is likely different, too, as this model should be able to corner faster, while also sitting a bit closer to the ground.
It looks like the fully electric BMW X5 M might come out sometime next year or maybe in 2028, as rumor has it that it could hit the assembly line in the latter year. That is also when its ICE-powered sibling might also come out of hiding, though to be honest, we wouldn’t be surprised if the automaker decides to unveil them a bit sooner.
What’s your take on the first-ever BMW X5 M Electric? Could this model convince you to spend your hard-earned money on it? Tell us all about it in the comments area below, and don’t forget to check it out in more detail in the photo gallery above.

2025 Cadillac XT6 Hits the Market for Under Half the Price at 11,400 Miles. Steal or Deal?
27 photos
Photo: eBay
This 2025 Cadillac XT6 was listed for sale for half the sticker, even though it has logged under 11,400 miles in less than a year since rolling off the production line. However, it’s not all good news. The vehicle was crashed and repaired, and is now for sale with a Rebuilt title.
"Loaded with features." This is how the seller describes this 2025 Cadillac XT6 Platinum Premium Luxury, right before a long list of equipment. The crossover came with Super Cruise and Night Vision, front bucket seats, front and rear heated seats, a heated steering wheel, automatic multi-zone climate control, keyless entry and start, navigation, hands-free power liftgate, and a cabin wrapped in leather and suede, and the list goes on and on.
Inside that cabin, airbags were deployed just a few months ago. Photos in a previous listing, where it was sold for $14,500, show the steering wheel cut open by the airbag deployment and the knee airbag hanging in the footwell.
The front passenger's airbag also inflated, while the rear side curtain airbags snapped to protect the heads of the occupants. And that doesn’t tell half the story. The Cadillac XT6 was involved in a collision that severely deformed the front end.
Photo: America Auto The front lower trim came apart, the grille was shattered, the bumper was cracked and contorted, while the hood was crumpled backwards. The driver's door was also damaged. Furthermore, a photo of the engine bay shows that it obviously needed internal work as well.
The engine block seems intact, but the large radiator, the front fascia, and headlight brackets (possibly headlights as well), along with the cooling fans and hood latch assembly, must have been replaced due to either cracking or misalignment caused by the accident that pushed them inward.
Luckily, the car did run and drive even after the crash, which means that the 3.6-liter V6 engine, code-named LGX, escaped the front of the impact. The V6 produces 310 horsepower (314 metric horsepower) and 271 pound-feet (367 Newton meters) of torque.
That is what makes the vehicle accelerate from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 6.9 seconds on its way to a top speed of 132 mph (212 kph). A nine-speed GM Hydra-Matic automatic transmission puts the power down through the front wheels. The gearbox also escaped intact.
Photo: America Auto The accident took place just months after the XT6 had been delivered, at 11,316 miles (18,211 kilometers), as indicated by the photos taken right after the crash, which makes it still a new car. But it is a new car with a Salvage title that was rebuilt to factory specification, which makes it look like it just rolled off the production line.
Cadillac discontinued the XT6 , which leaves the used car market as the only source for the model. A dealer is selling the repaired Cadillac, now having 11,414 miles (18,369 kilometers) on the clock, for $31,995. When new, the 2025 Cadillac XT6 Platinum Premium Luxury with Front Wheel Drive started at $66,290, which means this vehicle is for sale for under half the original sticker price. The seller is offering it with a Rebuilt Title that can be registered in all 50 states.

Forgotten Legends: 5 Defunct American Carmakers and Their Greatest Production Models
11 photos
Photo: RM Sotheby's
Before Detroit’s trio or giant corporations took control of the American automotive industry, some smaller yet exciting independent carmakers produced models that remain fascinating nearly a century later.
After the Second World War concluded, General Motors , the Ford Motor Company and the Chrysler Corporation took control of the industry and slowly absorbed or pushed out remaining independent brands.
However, before these three corporations became industry giants, America had several other established manufacturers that produced impressive vehicles.
Decades after closing their gates, most of these brands have been forgotten so today, we’re going to remember five of the most important defunct American carmakers and rediscover their most fascinating production models.
Packard and the Packard Twin Six Photo: Bonhams When we think about a iconic American luxury carmaker, the first brand that usually comes to mind is Cadillac. However, during the first half of the 20th century, the undisputed champion of American automotive luxury was Packard .
The company was founded in 1899 by brothers James Ward and William Packard, along with close friend and business partner George Lewis Weiss.
Initially, Packard built cars in Warren, Ohio but by 1903, after securing funds from a group of wealthy investors, the carmaker moved to a larger, state-of-the-art facility in Detroit where it grew into a standard-setting manufacturer.
Packard thrived throughout the 1920s when it was the best-selling luxury car manufacturer in the world, but the Great Depression years had a hugely negative impact on sales and the company never fully recovered. On its last legs, the company merged with Studebaker in 1954 but rather than reviving the brand, that merger ended up burring Packard just two years later.
Photo: Bonhams Throughout its history, Packard built several memorable cars, but unquestionably its most iconic was the Twin Six.
The model was introduced in late 1915 as a 1916 model and it is now widely recognized as the industry’s fist mass-produced V12-powered production car .
One of the greatest, most saught-afer luxury cars of its era, the Twin Six was produced until 1923, then the name was briefly revived in 1932 for a rather unsuccessful successor.
Throughout its lifespan, the model was offered with a wide range of factory and coach-built bodies that ranged from long, seven-passenger limousines to compact, two-door roadsters.
Duesenberg and the Duesenberg Model J Photo: Mecum Auctions Another important luxury carmaker that made waves around the globe before Cadillac was Duesenberg.
The company was founded in 1913 by German-born brothers Frederick “ Fred ” and August “ Augie ” Duesenberg in Saint Paul, Minnesota where they began developing race car, butt moved to Indianapolis, Indiana in 1920 to be closer to America’s most famous race track.
Though the brand had its roots in motorsport , it began building some of the most impressive luxury road cars shortly after the move to Indianapolis and quickly became one of the industry’s most famous names.
Duesenberg enjoyed great success during the during the second part of the 1920s and first half of the 1930s, but struggled to survive the Great Depression era and went under in 1937. A few revival attempts were made but, unfortunately, Duesenberg never rose from its ashes.
Photo: Gooding & Company Despite disappearing in 1937, the brand is very much alive in the hearts and mind of pre-war automotive enthusiasts, largely due to its most successful production series, the Model J.
Produced from 1928 to 1937, the Model J was a legendary mix between a full-blown luxury automobile and a proper race car.
Available in a wide range of body styles and powered by potent versions of the company’s technologically-advanced straight-eight, the Model J was in more ways than one, a precursor of the modern-day grand tourer
Unquestionably the most famous member of the Mode J line was the SSJ (shown above), a low-volume, high-performance, short-wheelbase version that featured the industry’s first supercharged engine capable of delivering 400 hp.
Pierce-Arrow and the Pierce-Arrow Silver Arrow Photo: RM Sotheby's Along with Packard, Pierce-Arrow was once a world-renown luxury carmaker that delivered some of the most impressive luxury automobiles of their respective eras.
The carmaker was founded in 1865 as Heinz, Pierce and Munschauer, but in the early days, it didn’t build cars. Instead, the company gilded household items and delicate birdcages.
George Norman Pierce went on to buy out his partners, renamed the company and switched to bicycle manufacturing , then in 1901, it began building cars.
By the late 1920s and early 1930s, Pierce-Arrow was one of the most renown luxury carmakers on the globe, but its refusal to adapt to the Great Depression era and build affordable vehicles led to its demise in 1938.
Photo: RM Sotheby's During its glory years, the carmaker developed several legendary models, of which the most iconic was the Silver Arrow.
Introduced at the 1933 New York Auto Show and produced in low quantities throughout that year, the model became famous for its lavishness and its futuristic streamlined fastback body . Simply put, there was nothing quite like it on the roads in 1933.
Though produced in very low numbers, the Silver Arrow remains the pinnacle of Pierce-Arrow luxury and innovation and surviving examples usually sell for millions of dollars on the rare occasions they pop up on the auction block.
Hudson and the Hudson Hornet Photo: RM Sotheby's The Hudson Motor Car Company was established in 1909 in Detroit and throughout its history it was one of the smaller independent carmakers that managed to be successful and put up a fight against the Motor City’s Big Three brands.
The company’s first production car, dubbed Model 20, was introduced in 1910 and became instantly successful as over 4,000 units were sold during its debut year.
Hudson survived the Great Depression era but never rose to the same level of success it enjoyed during the late 1920s. It eventually merged with Nash-Kelvinator in 1954, forming the American Motors Corporation (AMC) , but the brand name was discontinued in 1957.
Photo: RM Sotheby's Though Hudson reached its peak in terms of sales in the late 1920s, its most iconic production model, the first-generation Hornet, was produced from 1951 to 1954.
Offered in several body styles, the Hornet pioneered a unibody construction called " Monobilt ,” which drastically improved maneuverability. Moreover, the car was available with a massive 308 cubic-inch (5.0-liter) flathead straight-six which, depending on the setup, could produce over 200 hp, making the car more potent than V8-powered siblings.
The Hudson Hornet remains iconic for its undisputed dominance of the early NASCAR years, winning the Grand National manufacturer title three years in a row, from 1951 to 1953.
Auburn and the Auburn 851 “Boattail” Speedster Photo: Broad Arrow Auctions Founded in 1903 Auburn, Indiana by brothers Frank and Morris Eckhart, the company evolved from a successful carriage manufacturer into one of the country most daring and pioneering carmakers.
By the late 1920s and early 1930s, Auburn was renown for its impressive styling and also the performance potential of its models, which were among the world’s most sought-after sports cars.
Unfortunately, like all the other carmakers on this list, the Great Depression had a severe impact on the company and unable to properly recover, it disappeared in 1937.
Photo: Broad Arrow Auctions Despite its unfortunate demise, Auburn still inspires many enthusiasts with a soft spot for pre-war icons.
It’s most famous model, an undisputable automotive masterpiece, was the Auburn 851 “Boattail” Speedster, produced from 1928 to 1935 in three distinct series.
The car was available in several configurations, but the most famous was the low-volume supercharged version (SC), which featured a 4.6-liter (280 cubic inch) Lycoming flathead straight-eight rated at 150 hp.
Beautiful, fast, and surprisingly maneuverable, the Auburn 851 “Boattail” Speedster remains one of the finest pre-war sports cars built in the US.

One-Off Coupe-Cabriolet Based on the Alfa Romeo Giulia Quadrifoglio GTA Is Available for a Collector
6 photos
Photo: Carrozzeria Castagna Milano / Instagram
The Carrozzeria Castagna Milano, an Italian atelier company, revealed a tribute to the 2026 Paris Motor Show earlier this month, and it's up for grabs as a one-off coupe-cabriolet model based on the Alfa Romeo Giulia Quadrifoglio GTA , dedicated to a discerning collector.
The Carrozzeria Castagna Milano is one of the more obscure Italian atelier companies out there – the few sources don’t even agree about the company's origins. Some believe the company was founded in 1849 by Carlo Castagna; others say it goes further back to a Milanese carriage manufacturer named Paolo Mainetti, founded in 1835.
Anyway, Carlo Castagna managed to take over the business and, since 1905, switched to automobile fabrication, with the company revived twice during the 1990s and most recently focusing on models from Stellantis like the Fiat 500. Now, as it turns out, they’re upgrading to the high-performance Alfa Romeo Giulia Quadrifoglio GTA, which has a 2.9-liter V6 under the hood rocking 533 hp and 443 lb-ft of torque or 600 Nm, enough to sprint to 62 mph or 100 kph in 3.6 seconds and reach 186 mph or 300 kph.
Their latest bespoke project was announced initially on October 11, just prior to the start of the 2026 Paris Motor Show in France at the Paris Expo Porte de Versailles, acting as a one-off coupe-cabriolet tribute to the Mondial de l’Automobile based on the GTA. It’s available for an Alfa Romeo collector, but initially the company only showed a few teasers of the vehicle.
Now, though, we have the full-body renderings and additional details, including the fact that the vehicle can be homologated for the road and built in the short term. The car is 4,700 mm (185 inches) long, but only has two seats – which move back a full 330 mm (13 in.), making room for a much longer hood but also retaining a generous trunk capacity: 623 liters or 22 cubic foot.
The body has been reworked in carbon fiber, partially exposed, with some of the panels printed in 3D, and the weight of the car should come down to just 1,420 kg (3,131 lbs) “for an outstanding power-to-weight ratio, paired with revised final-drive gearing.” All the glass elements are also new, and “with the top up, the roof flows into triangular flying buttresses ending in fin-shaped tails that land on the central carbon fiber shadow of the trunk lid.”
With the roof down, the roof is said to disappear completely: “all that remains in view are the fairings rising from the seats, and the line stays clean, like a barchetta’s. This is perhaps the toughest challenge of the project, and Castagna states it openly: this car was designed to be a stunning coupé when closed, and an open car that never looks like a roofless derivative.” Cool or not?
